summary: Caveau Point rear range light at Cheticamp, Cape Breton: lit 1897 with the front light; keepers from Germain Chiasson; a 1912 lifeboat station beside it; Coast Guard property, closed.

light.note: Front light: F R, focal height 16.8 m, range 14 nm (CCG list). Both lights fixed red now. Both were fixed white until 1950 (LF).

structures.type: square tower, white with a red vertical stripe
structures.note: Enclosed tower built around 1990 (LF; Rowlett). NSLPS lists the rear in 1989 as a white structure with a red stripe, 8.2 m high.

structures.type: square skeleton tower, white daymark with red vertical stripe
structures.note: Replaced the original wooden tower (1897). LF and Rowlett: 1976; NSLPS: 1973 to 1980.

access.note: Site and tower closed. Rowlett: private property, visible from the Cabot Trail road. LF: grounds and tower closed.

events.note: Two leading lights put in operation 3 Oct 1897 (LF, quoting the Department). Rowlett and NSLPS also give 1897.
N. D. Desveaux placed in charge (LF). Marine keepers table gives appointment 27 April 1912.
Separate Life-Saving Service station at Cheticamp, with a boat-house near Aucoin's wharf and a lookout tower about 183 m (600 ft) from the range lights; crew from Oct 1912 (Department report, 1914).
Vessel stranded at Cheticamp on 1 Oct 1912. Formal investigation at Montreal, 10 Oct, cause an unknown and unmarked shoal. Ship not named here. Location given only as Cheticamp.
Sixth-order dioptric lens in use 1922 to 1941 (NSLPS, front light).
Range lights changed from fixed white to fixed green (LF).
Skeletal towers replaced the original wooden towers (LF; Rowlett). NSLPS gives 1973 to 1980 for the front light.
Enclosed tower built for the rear light, around 1990 (LF; Rowlett). NSLPS lists it in 1989.

keepers.name: Germain Chiasson

keepers.name: Severin F. Chaisson

wrecks.vessel: not named in the report entry read
wrecks.outcome: Stranded at Cheticamp, Cape Breton. Formal investigation at Montreal, 10 Oct 1912, by Commander Lindsay: stranding due to striking an unknown and unmarked shoal; master exonerated. The report does not say where at Cheticamp.

corrections.why: Rowlett gives ARLHS CAN-1314 for the front range light and CAN-123 for the rear. The record's CAN1314 is the front light's number.
Rowlett gives NGA 8804 for the front range light and NGA 8808 for the rear. The record's 8804 is the front light's number.

1976 is the year both range lights were given skeletal towers (LF, Rowlett; NSLPS gives 1973 to 1980 for the front). The rear light's present enclosed tower dates from around 1990 (LF, Rowlett) and NSLPS lists it by 1989.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1976 (record, Rowlett) is when the range lights received skeletal towers in place of the wooden originals. The rear light's enclosed tower is later: around 1990 (LF, Rowlett) or 1989 (NSLPS). The story gives both.
Rowlett gives 31 m (103 ft); the Coast Guard list gives 29.2 m. The Coast Guard list is the official current figure and is used.
Heights: Coast Guard 8.5 m; NSLPS 8.2 m (1989); Rowlett 8 m (27 ft). The Coast Guard list is used.

notes_for_editor: 1) Keepers from Department tables are read by column position from OCR. (a) Germain Chiasson at Caveau Point Range: the 1911 statement (scan p. 256, printed p. 254) and the 1906 list (scan p. 180) put the name against the station; both were checked against the page images on 2026-10-28, and the name sits on the Caveau Point Range Lights row (1906 list, printed p. 171). (b) N. D. Desveaux, appointed 27 April 1912, is matched by position between R. McDonald (Carter Island) and A. Richard (Charlo harbour range) in the 1916 table (scan p. 76, printed p. 69) and the 1915 keeper list. The page image was checked on 2026-10-28: the Caveau point range row reads N. D. Desveaux, appointed April 27, 1912 (printed p. 69, fiscal 1914-15). (c) 'D. Desveaux' appointed 19 July 1912 in the same table is not linked to Caveau in the story. 2) The 1897 construction account is LF's quotation of the Department's annual report for 1897-98. That report is not in the local corpus (its series starts in 1900), so the quotation was not checked against the original. 3) The Cheticamp life-saving station (1912) is a separate Life-Saving Service station, not the range lights. The 1912 stranding is recorded under Cheticamp only; the story does not tie it to Caveau shoal. The printed entry (p. 187) gives no vessel name, and the story names none. 4) NSLPS lists the front light's 'Still Operating' as No, but the Coast Guard list gives F R for both lights. The story follows the Coast Guard list. 5) Lighthouse Friends and the Lighthouse Directory disagree on the 1950 and 1976 changes and on the rear light's year (1976 vs about 1990). The story gives both. 6) The record's aton CAN1314 and NGA 8804 belong to the front light per Rowlett; the rear light's values are CAN-123 and NGA 8808. The record's Wikidata 'wood' material for the rear is not confirmed by the Coast Guard list (which gives white square tower). 7) Living people: Gregoire Patrick Lefort (LF: at least 1964) and the 1931-46 keepers are named as LF prints them, with no details beyond those. 8) Length: the keeper record is names and dates only and the Lighthouse Friends page is the main narrative source, so the story stays near 900 words rather than the rich range. The Rowlett focal plane of 31 m conflicts with the CCG 29.2 m; the CCG list is used. 9) Canadian Marine reports list the Cheticamp life-saving expenditure in a table; the figure ($5,620.01) sits on the Cheticamp row (printed p. 225) and was checked against the page image on 2026-10-28.
